sentences: The format is V# word3[18:12] (GFX10_FORMAT, from Mesa's `gfx10-rsrc.json`, saved as `tools\gfx10_formats.json`).

The 8- and 16-bit UINT/SINT formats 5, 6, 11, 12, 18, 19, 28, 61 and 70 were missing until 2026-11-22 and read 0: UINT channels zero-extend, SINT channels sign-extend, d16 packs them as 16-bit integers, measured natively on gfx1036 (wave32 and wave64) with `tools/hw_oracle` and checked word for word by `tests/semantic/test_buffer_format_narrow_int.py`; GPU-checked by `runtime/test/shaders/cs_fmt_int_narrow.asm`, whose 136 expected words are the same program run natively on gfx1036 (exact on an RTX 5080 and on the gfx1036 iGPU through Vulkan).
Full-width SINT accesses preserve integer bits.
D16 SINT loads saturate to signed 16-bit and D16 stores sign-extend, covered by the synthetic `cs_fmt_sint32.asm` readback.
DST_SEL swizzle is applied (0→0, 1→1.0f for float/norm or integer 1 for UINT/SINT, 4..7→X..W).
Missing channels repeat the format's own (component *c* = *c* mod *n*), measured on an RX 6700 (SHADER-86).
UNORM/SNORM give the correctly rounded quotient by (2ⁿ−1), as the hardware does (0 mismatches vs hardware over 395,776 conversions on that GPU).

It is built with integer ops (`Gen.norm_bits`): x/(2ⁿ−1) in binary is x's bits repeated, so a 64-bit multiply by the repeat pattern, `FindUMsb` and the round bit give the f32 exactly (the tail never ends, so there are no ties).
`OpFDiv` is not enough on the GPU: Vulkan allows it 2.5 ULP, and on an RX 6700 (AMD Windows 26.11.2) and an RTX 5090 it returned the reciprocal-multiply bits (8_UNORM 130/256 exact, #599).

Checked against exact values in `tests/semantic/test_norm_decode.py` (every value up to 8 bits, edges and the reciprocal-multiply misses for 10, 15 and 16 bits). 8_SNORM (2), 16_SNORM (8) and 8_8_SNORM (15) were missing until 2026-11-22 and decoded to 0.
Format names list the channel widths from the top bit, so `2_10_10_10` (50) is R10G10B10A2 and `10_10_10_2` (44) has a 2-bit x (Mesa `gfx10_format_table.py`, `ac_formats.c`).
Until 2026-11-22 the two were swapped, in stores too.

Until 2026-11-21 an element that started mid-dword re-read dword 0 for its tail (`need` was `ceil(size/4)` and only the first dword was shifted); loads now take `need = ceil((byte_shift + size) / 4)` dwords and shift the whole window so the packed stream starts at the element (FUZZ-5, leftover from #234).
The 10:10:10:2 order is checked by `cs_fmt_1010102` in `tests/semantic/test_value_semantics.py` (the shader decodes the format, so a GPU run can't check it).
Mid-dword spanning elements are checked by `tests/semantic/test_buffer_load_format.py` (`CrossingDwordBoundary`); repeat / UNORM / DST_SEL 1 by the SHADER-86 cases in the same file.

The `_xy` and `_xyz` forms (buffer and tbuffer) are GPU-checked by `cs_fmt_xy_xyz.asm`, whose words were measured natively on a Radeon 680M (gfx1035, RDNA2): they write only their 2 or 3 VGPRs, and missing channels repeat there too (TEST-185).
